mandatory_modal_verb.note: The only acceptable modal for binding requirements per ARP4754A and DO-178C writing conventions.

ears_patterns.description: EARS (Easy Approach to Requirements Syntax) patterns for rewriting requirements. The recommender agent SHALL choose the most appropriate pattern based on the requirement nature.
ears_patterns.reference: Mavin et al., EARS (Easy Approach to Requirements Syntax), IEEE RE 2009.

patterns.name: Ubiquitous
patterns.use_when: The requirement applies always, unconditionally, with no trigger or precondition.
patterns.example: The Flight Control System shall respond to pilot inputs within 20 ms.

patterns.name: Event-Driven
patterns.template: WHEN <trigger> [<optional precondition>], the <system name> shall <system response>.
patterns.use_when: The requirement is triggered by a discrete event or stimulus.
patterns.example: WHEN the pilot applies a control input, the Flight Control System shall generate a surface deflection command within 20 ms.

patterns.name: Unwanted Behavior
patterns.template: IF <unwanted condition or event>, THEN the <system name> shall <system response>.
patterns.use_when: The requirement specifies the system response to a fault, failure, or off-nominal condition.
patterns.example: IF a sensor failure is detected, THEN the Flight Control System shall switch to the redundant sensor within 50 ms.

patterns.name: State-Driven
patterns.template: WHILE <system state>, the <system name> shall <system response>.
patterns.use_when: The requirement applies continuously during a specific operating state or mode.
patterns.example: WHILE in degraded mode, the Flight Control System shall maintain attitude control with an accuracy of ±2°.

patterns.name: Optional Feature
patterns.template: WHERE <feature is included>, the <system name> shall <system response>.
patterns.use_when: The requirement applies only when an optional feature or configuration is present.
patterns.example: WHERE the enhanced autopilot feature is installed, the Flight Control System shall provide envelope protection.

patterns.name: Complex
patterns.template: (Combination of two or more EARS patterns above.)
patterns.use_when: The requirement involves multiple triggers, states, or conditions that cannot be cleanly separated without losing meaning.
patterns.example: WHILE in cruise mode, WHEN the autopilot is engaged, the Flight Control System shall maintain altitude within ±50 ft.

rules.title: Unique requirement identifier
rules.objective: Ensure each requirement is uniquely identifiable
checks: Verify the requirement has an identifier
Verify the identifier is unique across the requirement set
Verify the identifier adheres to the project naming convention

rules.title: Unambiguous requirement wording
rules.objective: Eliminate ambiguity — every term must be defined or measurable
checks: Detect terms from the ambiguous-term categories below and flag each with its category and remediation:
[performance_speed / HIGH] fast, slow, quickly, soon, rapidly, timely — specify a numeric latency, throughput, or response time with unit and tolerance
[quantitative_approximation / HIGH] approximately, about, around, roughly — specify an exact value ± tolerance
[vague_quantification / HIGH] adequate, sufficient, appropriate, suitable, negligible — define the objective measurable criterion
[conditional_applicability / HIGH] as required, if applicable, where necessary, when needed — state the condition explicitly using IF/WHEN/WHILE/WHERE
[subjective_quality_judgment / HIGH] good, bad, better, best, optimal, acceptable, reasonable — replace with a measurable threshold
[performance_attributes / HIGH] reliable, robust, flexible, efficient — decompose into measurable sub-requirements
[usability_attributes / HIGH] user-friendly, intuitive, easy, simple — specify a measurable usability criterion
[optimization_terms / HIGH] minimize, maximize — specify the target value or bound
[state_classification / HIGH] normal, abnormal — define the specific operating condition explicitly
[scale_references / HIGH] high, low, large, small — specify a numeric threshold with unit
[technology_references / MEDIUM] state-of-the-art — reference a specific technical standard or document

rules.title: Operational modes specified
rules.objective: Ensure applicability conditions are stated
checks: Verify operational modes or conditions are explicitly stated
Flag missing or implicit operational assumptions
Verify behavior during mode transitions is explicitly defined

rules.title: Acceptance criteria defined
rules.objective: Ensure requirement can be accepted objectively
checks: Detect measurable criteria or referenced verification method
Flag requirements without acceptance criteria

rules.title: Safety requirements reference DAL
rules.objective: Ensure safety requirements reference failure conditions and DAL
checks: Identify safety-related requirements
Verify associated failure condition and DAL are specified

rules.title: Requirement source identified
rules.objective: Ensure traceability to origin
checks: Verify presence of source or rationale
Classify source (regulatory, customer, derived)

rules.title: Derived requirements justified
rules.objective: Ensure derived requirements are documented and safety-routed
checks: Identify derived requirements
Verify justification or derivation rationale exists
Verify derived requirements are routed to the safety process (FHA/PSSA) for hazard evaluation

rules.title: Coverage of system functions
rules.objective: Ensure all FHA functions are covered by requirements
checks: Compare requirement coverage against FHA functions
Identify missing functional coverage

rules.title: Interface requirements completeness
rules.objective: Ensure interfaces are fully specified
checks: Verify protocols, data formats, and timing are defined
Flag partially specified interfaces
Verify system response to invalid inputs, out-of-range data, or missing signals is defined (Robustness)

rules.title: Environmental requirements specified
rules.objective: Ensure environmental constraints are stated where applicable
checks: Detect environmental constraints applicability
Verify explicit limits are defined

rules.title: No contradictory requirements
rules.objective: Eliminate logical contradictions across the requirement set
checks: Perform pairwise semantic contradiction analysis
Flag conflicting constraints or behaviors
Flag semantic equivalence (duplicate requirements)
Flag subsuming requirements (one requirement fully contained in another)

rules.title: Consistent terminology
rules.objective: Ensure uniform use of terms across the requirement set
checks: Extract key terms from all requirements
Detect inconsistent usage or definitions of the same term
Verify terms against the approved project Data Dictionary or Glossary

rules.title: Consistent units and tolerances
rules.objective: Prevent unit or tolerance mismatches across requirements
checks: Detect physical quantities and their units in all requirements
Verify unit and tolerance consistency across the requirement set

rules.title: Consistent DAL allocation
rules.objective: Ensure DAL assignments are consistent with safety assessments
checks: Compare DAL assignments with FHA/PSSA
Flag any mismatch between assigned DAL and failure condition severity

rules.title: Performance feasibility
rules.objective: Ensure performance requirements are consistent with known HW/SW constraints
checks: Compare performance requirements with HW/SW constraints
Flag infeasible or contradictory performance requirements

rules.title: Timing consistency
rules.objective: Ensure timing constraints do not conflict across requirements
checks: Extract all timing constraints from the requirement set
Detect conflicting latency, period, or deadline requirements

rules.title: Requirement is verifiable
rules.objective: Ensure objective verification is possible
checks: Verify a verification approach exists for the requirement
Reject unverifiable statements that cannot be tested, analysed, inspected, or demonstrated

rules.title: Quantified performance thresholds
rules.objective: Ensure performance criteria are measurable
checks: Detect numeric thresholds and tolerances in the requirement
Flag vague performance statements that lack numeric criteria (value + unit + tolerance)

rules.title: No subjective terms without measurable backing
rules.objective: Eliminate purely subjective requirements
checks: Detect subjective or qualitative wording
Verify that measurable acceptance criteria exist for every subjective term

rules.title: Verification method mapped
rules.objective: Ensure a verification method is identified for the requirement
checks: Verify mapping to at least one of: Test (T), Analysis (A), Inspection (I), Demonstration (D)
Verify the specific phase or level of verification is identified (e.g. equipment level, system level, flight test)

rules.title: Verification feasibility
rules.objective: Ensure verification can realistically be performed
checks: Assess feasibility of the required verification against project test capabilities and constraints

rules.title: No impossible verification conditions
rules.objective: Avoid undefined or impossible states in the requirement
checks: Detect physically impossible states or undefined references in the requirement text

rules.title: Traceability to higher-level requirements
rules.objective: Ensure upward traceability to parent or regulatory source
checks: Verify link to aircraft-level, regulatory, or customer requirement
Identify orphaned requirements that have no parent trace

rules.title: Derived requirement traceability
rules.objective: Ensure derived requirements are traceable to their justification
checks: Verify link to safety assessment (FHA/PSSA/SSA) or documented design decision

rules.title: Downward traceability
rules.objective: Ensure every requirement links to implementation artifacts
checks: Verify trace to design or code elements exists
Ensure 100% downward coverage — no requirement may lack downstream allocation

rules.title: HW/SW allocation documented
rules.objective: Ensure hardware/software allocation is specified for each requirement
checks: Verify that HW/SW allocation documentation exists for the requirement

rules.title: FHA failure condition traceability
rules.objective: Ensure each FHA failure condition maps to at least one safety requirement
checks: Verify each FHA failure condition is covered by at least one safety requirement

rules.title: Correct system behavior
rules.objective: Ensure the requirement reflects the intended system behavior
checks: Compare requirement intent with the system definition
Verify adherence to known physical or mathematical boundaries

rules.title: No unnecessary design constraints
rules.objective: Avoid premature design decisions in requirements
checks: Detect implementation-specific wording (how the system does something)
Verify the requirement states what the system must do, not how it should be implemented

rules.title: Correct modal verb — 'shall' mandatory
rules.objective: Ensure 'shall' is the sole modal for all binding obligations
checks: Verify 'shall' is used for every binding obligation
Flag any of the following weak or non-standard modals and replace with 'shall' if the obligation is binding:
should      — recommendation, not obligation
may         — permission, not obligation
might       — possibility, not obligation
could       — capability or possibility, not obligation
would       — conditional, not a binding obligation
can         — capability; use 'shall be capable of' for binding statements
must        — non-standard in ARP4754A context; replace with 'shall'
will        — expresses intent or future state, not a binding obligation
is required to — passive paraphrase; rewrite as active 'shall'
should be able to — doubly weak; replace with 'shall be capable of'

rules.title: Single obligation per statement
rules.objective: Avoid compound requirements — one 'shall' per statement
checks: Count the number of 'shall' occurrences — more than one indicates a compound requirement
Detect multiple obligations joined by 'and' or 'or' within a single statement
Split into separate requirements, one 'shall' per statement

rules.title: Appropriate abstraction level
rules.objective: Ensure the requirement is written at the correct hierarchy level
checks: Assess abstraction level relative to the requirement hierarchy (aircraft / system / item)

rules.title: Explicit assumptions
rules.objective: Ensure all assumptions underlying the requirement are documented
checks: Detect implicit assumptions embedded in the requirement text
Verify every assumption is explicitly stated

rulesets.description: Lexical wording rules — markers that unconditionally invalidate a requirement

rules.title: No TBD placeholders
rules.objective: Ensure all values are defined before review
checks: Detect the literal string 'TBD' (case-sensitive) anywhere in the requirement text
A requirement containing TBD is not ready for review — all values must be resolved before submission

rules.title: No TBC placeholders
rules.objective: Ensure all values are confirmed before review
checks: Detect the literal string 'TBC' (case-sensitive) anywhere in the requirement text
A requirement containing TBC is not ready for review — all values must be confirmed before submission

rulesets.origin: ARP4754A writing conventions + project wording guide
rulesets.description: Sentence structure and morphology rules — clarity, active voice, unambiguous reference

rules.title: No negation issues
rules.objective: Express obligations as positive, measurable statements
checks: [double_negation] Detect two negation markers in the same clause (e.g. 'shall not be inactive') — rewrite as a positive obligation
[hidden_negation] Detect implicit negative constructions ('unless', 'except when', 'unless otherwise specified') — make the condition explicit
[negative_requirement] Detect requirements expressed in negative form — prefer 'The X shall achieve Y' over 'The X shall not fail to achieve Y'

rules.title: No structural complexity
rules.objective: Keep each requirement simple, focused, and parseable
checks: [long_sentences] Flag sentences exceeding 30 words — split or restructure using an EARS pattern
[multiple_subordinate_clauses] Detect stacked dependent clauses — restructure using EARS patterns
[nested_conditions] Detect multiple embedded IF/WHEN/WHILE structures — decompose into separate requirements

rules.title: Unambiguous references and explicit subject
rules.objective: Every pronoun and reference must have a clear, named antecedent
checks: [ambiguous_pronouns] Detect 'it', 'this', 'that', 'they', 'them' without a clear antecedent — replace with the explicit subject name
[unclear_references] Detect 'the system' when multiple systems are in scope — name the specific system
[dangling_modifiers] Detect modifiers not clearly attached to the subject they qualify
[implicit_subject] Verify the grammatical subject of 'shall' is an identifiable system or function — not 'it', 'this', or omitted

rules.title: Active voice
rules.objective: Use active voice to make the obligated entity explicit
checks: Detect agentless passive constructions: 'shall be <past-participle>', 'is <past-participle> by'
Rewrite as '<Named subject> shall <verb> <object>'

rules.title: No mixed modality
rules.objective: Use a single, consistent modal within each requirement statement
checks: Detect the combination of 'shall' with 'should', 'may', or 'can' within the same requirement statement
Resolve to a single modal — use 'shall' if the obligation is binding

rules.title: No logical ambiguity
rules.objective: Make logical structure and conjunctions explicit and unambiguous
checks: [and_or_combination] Detect 'and/or' — choose one conjunction or split the requirement into two
[implicit_conditions] Detect conditions not explicitly introduced by IF, WHEN, WHILE, or WHERE — make them explicit
[temporal_ambiguity] Detect unclear sequences of events (e.g. 'after initialisation') — specify the exact trigger or duration

rules.title: No vagueness in structure
rules.objective: Ensure requirements are complete, closed, and self-standing
checks: [open_ended_lists] Detect 'etc.', 'etc', 'and/or', 'including but not limited to' — enumerate all items explicitly
[incomplete_sentences] Detect sentence fragments — ensure the requirement is a complete, self-standing statement

rules.title: Sentence length
rules.objective: Keep sentences concise for clarity and parsability
checks: Count words in the requirement statement
Flag if word count exceeds 30 — consider splitting or restructuring with an EARS pattern
